args.text:
KEY MESSAGE 2...Might cop the odd shower Wednesday, but drier overall. Dry weather's back for Thursday, and it'll be on the cool side for this time of year.

Pull up a stool. Wednesday, a trailing cold front shifts across the region, and surface high pressure builds in from the west through the day behind it. The model soundings show more mixing in the boundary layer, which backs up drier conditions, and westerlies too, gusting 20-30 mph (30-50 km/h), so hang on to your hat. Westerly, downslope flow on top of 925mb temperatures of +17- 18C means a warm autumn day, highs in the 70s (low to mid 20s C) in heaps of spots. Not bad for autumn, that. There's a hint of a stray shower or two as a weak wave wanders through, but it won't cover much ground, and with the lower levels that dry it'll be a light shower/sprinkle at most. Barely worth getting the brolly out.

Then the high settles in further into Thursday and the airmass dries out even more. Thursday's likely dry, though cooler than Wednesday. A cooler airmass will have moved in as well, with 925mb temperatures around 10C cooler than Wednesday. So you're looking at temperatures on the cool side for the season, mostly in the lower 60s (around 16C). Jumper weather.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Low pressure system expected to bring rain Friday into early Saturday. Gusty northwesterlies and temperatures below normal.

Now here's where it gets interesting. Deterministic and ensemble guidance both have a stronger/deeper northern stream shortwave trough shoving across the Great Lakes and the northeast Friday into Saturday. And this one's got synoptic support behind it: an upper level jet parks itself near southern New England, giving large scale ascent, and while it's at it, it's advecting a plume of above normal moisture north into the region. That sets the table for widespread rain. Plenty of moisture about, mind, but instability looks limited, so the chance of heavy rain impacts is kept down. Ensemble guidance has amounts mostly from 0.25 to 0.60" (6-15 mm), with the ECMWF and Canadian leaning wetter than the GFS solutions. Go by those particular models and amounts closer to an inch (25 mm) are possible. Those bigger totals aren't out of the question either, if we can tap into better forcing with the warm front. The finer details, like exactly when the rain rocks up and when it clears off, are less certain, cos the guidance still can't agree. Best bet is the rain lobs in the Friday morning timeframe and keeps at it overnight. Most guidance has this system fairly progressive, meaning it won`t be hanging about the whole weekend like a bad smell. The bulk of the rain likely clears out early Saturday morning. On top of all that, the initial southerly LLJ with this system nudges in Friday, and if it mixes down enough, it'll bring breezy to gusty southerlies (gusts 20-30 mph, or 30-50 km/h).

Then, by early Saturday morning, a strong cold front barrels across the region and drops the northeast into a classic cold air advection pattern: gusty NW winds, cooler temperatures and the odd isolated shower, the full catastrophe. A NW 40-50 kt LLJ sets up across the region Saturday. The tighter gradient, plus CAA helping steepen the lapse rates, backs up deeper mixing, and that means gusty NW winds. How much mixing we get and how strong the LLJ ends up are still less certain this far out, but the ensembles show a signal for gusts of 35-45 mph (55-70 km/h) possible, maybe higher out over the coastal waters. 925mb temperatures run between - 2C and +2C Saturday, which likely makes it the coldest of the season so far. Highs will likely battle to get out of the 40s (single figures C) across the interior, with low 50s (around 10-11C) in the valleys and coastal plain. RH fields show leftover moisture hanging round in the cyclonic flow pattern, and that may be enough for a few isolated showers. Some of the higher spots across the Berkshires may only hit the 40 degree mark (about 4C) on Saturday. Brass monkeys. It`s a bit too early to say the "S word" just yet (snow). But...if the timing lines up, a morning flurry or shower can`t be ruled out on that higher ground out west. Expect a cold night Saturday night, with a good chance the interior drops to at least freezing. The higher spots may drop into the upper 20s (around -2C). Rug up.

result.scope: Issues: flagged phrases, swearing over the cap, US spelling and US words. Warnings: the guide's style rules and swearing density; fidelity to the original (length, names, numbers). Not checked: invented slang.

declined.reason: 'northern stream' is the jet stream's northern branch, a term of art, not a watercourse.
Means going through hard times (of people); here temperatures 'struggle' to climb, so 'battle to get out of'.
